top_strength: Landon read an 80-year-old customer moving his handicapped wife out of a three-level condo and sold the two-day split as care rather than as upsell, which is exactly the right frame for this buyer: "my main reason for one to kind of go over two days is I wouldn't want it to go to one day and then it kinda just be something that kind of goes into the evening or anything like that. I wouldn't want to want, wouldn't want, have you guys, you know, out super late or anything." He then protected the customer's budget unprompted after hearing "we're on the social security income," telling him "easiest way to save money is just gonna be obviously to pack as much as you can and then kind of leave the moving part to us," and built the second day in as a contingency rather than a charge. The refrigerator-and-cooler advice was proactive FAQ handling of the kind that wins referrals, and the personal aside about his own move landed genuine rapport: "we even with just being there for three years we couldn't believe how long it have been and how much we could accumulate. So, I can only imagine I totally get it." The call closed booked, on dates, with the customer volunteering "I'm looking forward to working with you it sounds like you got a game."
coaching_note: Landon never asked for the addresses — on a call where he quoted $2,285 and booked two days, the origin and destination were never collected, and the one access detail the customer volunteered went unexplored: "it is on the sloping land, it's not severe but it does have slop to it," answered with "Okay." That is the single highest-risk gap here, because a three-level condo with a slope and a truck parked round the back is precisely the kind of carry that blows a five-to-seven-hour estimate — and estimate accuracy is the rock this grading feeds. The fix is mechanical: lock addresses and zips before inventory, then when a customer hands you a walk or slope detail, price it out loud ("that slope and the stairs from the middle level are what will move us toward the seven-hour end") so the number he hears is defended before move day rather than explained after it. Second, none of the three differentiators — No Worries, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee — appeared on a call that was already won on trust from his son's move; that was free margin left on the table.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and unhurried with an elderly customer who dominated the airtime, with real empathy markers ("Yeah, I get her set up. Get her a little bit of a better easier access, huh") and a self-deprecating personal story that built genuine rapport, held back from a 5 only by heavy "Okay, perfect / Mm-hmm" filler in place of substantive acknowledgment through the long inventory stretch.
